trust_decision.summary: One decision per HTTP request: may this client run phpSysInfo? read_config.php derives the client IP from the client-controlled X-Forwarded-For header, then the client-controlled Client-IP header, and only then from REMOTE_ADDR, and compares that value against the PSI_ALLOWED list; because the attacker-supplied headers outrank the socket address, any client can claim an allowlisted IPv4 address and pass the gate.

landing_point.why: The advisory names X-Forwarded-For and Client-IP; those header names occur exactly once in the whole tree, in this header-priority chain that feeds the PSI_ALLOWED comparison.

fix_sites.entry_point: index.php:32, js.php:24, language/language.php:42 and xml.php:32 (xml.php only via WebpageXML::__construct -> Output::_checkConfig, includes/output/class.Output.inc.php:52) all include read_config.php and therefore execute this gate
fix_sites.module_kind: shared bootstrap include (config loader + access gate), loaded by every PHP entry point

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The shipped phpsysinfo.ini.new is only a template that each operator edits per deployment, so a solver can treat the new trusted-proxy knob as documentation and implement the whole behaviour in read_config.php, leaving the deployed default unaware of TRUSTED_PROXIES.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Reverse-proxy deployment: when REMOTE_ADDR is the proxy's own address, the real client address exists only in X-Forwarded-For / Client-IP. Removing the header branch (the fastest fix) fails closed and denies every legitimate proxied client that PSI_ALLOWED is supposed to admit, and it leaves the already-broken multi-hop case permanently broken - a list in X-Forwarded-For makes ip2long fail, so the request is denied outright at read_config.php:53-57.

O6_input_shapes: comma-separated X-Forwarded-For list, right-most element taken as the candidate
TRUSTED_PROXIES entry as a bare IPv4 address
TRUSTED_PROXIES entry as a CIDR network
non-IP candidate value (rejected by ip2long, request falls back to REMOTE_ADDR instead of dying)
no proxy headers present (REMOTE_ADDR used directly)

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: tools/README calls it a test utility ('Displays anonymized /proc/cpuinfo'), so it reads as an admin script to delete rather than a phpSysInfo page the allowlist covers
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 package (tools/ vs repository root), 0 intervening files

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: documented in tools/README as a distribution-testing helper ('Generates a txt file for distribution testing'), i.e. a developer tool, not the monitored application
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 package (tools/ vs repository root), 0 intervening files

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: documented as a PHP environment check-up helper ('Displays information about PHP'); it leaks fingerprint data rather than host state, so a solver can argue the allowlist never covered it
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 package (tools/ vs repository root), 0 intervening files

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A shared clientIp() resolver placed next to the existing readenv() $_SERVER accessor, used by a second consumer (an access/audit line or a plugin) as well as by the gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: readenv() is already the project's generic server-variable reader, so a maintainer refactoring the trusted-proxy logic would naturally grow a helper here and call it from more than one place, giving the same mechanism two call sites in different packages

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An ALLOWED gate added to the only web-reachable script that serves files without bootstrapping the config
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: css.php is the one script under templates/ that is called directly by URL and never includes read_config.php; a maintainer extending it to serve templated parameters or images would plausibly bolt the same check on

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A 'require PSI_APP_ROOT/read_config.php' guard at the top of the host-information diagnostic scripts
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: these scripts ship inside the web root and print host data, so a maintainer who noticed the gap after this advisory would plausibly close it there too, in a separate package from the gate

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second defaults-file knob (for example a per-feature restriction or a proxy-list variant) that only takes effect if the config loader's type coercion in read_config.php is understood
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every security-relevant switch in this project is a MAIN-section ini key coerced by read_config.php:27-34, so adding the sibling in the template and forgetting the loader (or the reverse) is the project's own idiom

O9_family: authorization bypass by spoofed client identity (IP allowlist bypass)

O10_build.language: PHP (>=5.1.3 declared; Dockerfile:14 installs PHP 7.4 with Apache)
O10_build.toolchain: none - plain PHP, no build step and no composer install (composer.json:6-18 declares only php and ext-* requirements)
O10_build.project_tests: none - the only CI is PHP lint across 5.5-8.4 (.github/workflows/phplint.yml:22-43); no test/spec directory and no test covering read_config.php in the pinned tree

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Drop the X-Forwarded-For / Client-IP branch entirely and read REMOTE_ADDR only - it stops the bypass but silently denies every legitimate client that sits behind a reverse proxy.

out_of_scope_notes: xml.php:42 echoes $_GET['callback'] straight after a /[^\w\?]/ test when JSONP mode is enabled - a reflected-script concern in a different protection than this advisory's allowlist; not pursued.
unverified: Repository size in MB could not be measured (no shell in this session), so O4.repo_mb is null and tiny_repo was not asserted; the tree has 1110 files, mostly gfx/*.png, with about 85 PHP files.
Nothing was executed: every route and line above was established by reading the pinned tree, not by running phpSysInfo.

Gate reachability is by reading only: index.php:32 and js.php:24 require read_config.php directly, language/language.php:42 includes it, and xml.php:32 reaches it indirectly through WebpageXML::__construct (includes/output/class.WebpageXML.inc.php:269-271) calling Output::_checkConfig (includes/output/class.Output.inc.php:52).

O1 counts the four entry points that execute the flawed header-priority resolution; only index.php and xml.php serve host information, while js.php and language/language.php serve static assets through the same gate.

phpsysinfo.ini.new is a shipped config template rather than source, so it is counted in O2 and j_sites_touched but not in fix_sites; the published fix edits it at fix.diff:5-28 and the code at fix.diff:37-92.
tools/checkdistro.php also runs without the allowlist but iterates sample/distrotest, which is absent from the pinned tree, so it exposes nothing on a stock deployment and was not listed in O8.

Whether a hidden test can drive the trusted-proxy branch offline is unconfirmed; with a local server REMOTE_ADDR is 127.0.0.1, so TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1 plus a spoofed X-Forwarded-For would exercise it, but this was not run.
present_in_latest is 'unknown' for all O8 routes because the brief states there is no latest release to compare against.
